author: GameSpot YouTube
text:
Star Wars Zero Company Is Good But Seems To Play Things Too Safe - Preview
I was hoping "XCOM but Star Wars" would have been a little bit more than just Star Wars painted over XCOM.

I'm a bit bummed that I don't like Star Wars Zero Company more than I do. The upcoming turn-based-tactics game is set during my absolute favorite moment in the Star Wars' timeline, The Clone Wars, and games that are just like it--like XCOM: Chimera Squad and Marvel's Midnight Suns--are some of my most-played games in recent years. If pressed, I'd tell you that Zero Company is a good game (or at least, the four hours of it I've played are good). But of what I've seen so far, there's nothing about the game that makes it really stand out from its peers. Zero Company seems to play things too safe, sticking to a tried-and-true formula that works.

Opening Magic: The Gathering HOBBIT Collector Boosters
The Hobbit marks a major milestone for the Universes Beyond initiative within Magic: The Gathering, as it is the first “sequel” to a previous UB product, The Lord Of The Rings.

Despite The Hobbit being only one novel, as opposed to the trilogy of The Lord of the Rings, the team found that there was still ample material in order to build out their set. The approach, because of that smaller source material size, was to get as granular as possible.
